description: PowSyBl (Power System Blocks) is an open-source framework written in Java for building software for power system simulation and analysis. PowSyBl Core provides the network data model and the building blocks on which applications for load flow, security and sensitivity analysis, network import and export and grid studies are written, and its modular design lets developers extend or customise features. The project belongs to the LF Energy Foundation, a Linux Foundation project for open-source innovation in the energy and electricity sectors, and is governed by a technical steering committee. It is not tied to one country: any transmission or distribution network that can be imported can be studied. Source code is on GitHub (latest core tag v7.4.0 release candidate, commits to 22 September 2026), with tutorials on read-the-docs and a project site at powsybl.org, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 at no cost. Caveats: PowSyBl Core is not a standalone application, so users need Java development skills or a companion application, and the README notes that ready-to-run demos are not yet downloadable. Simulation uses are network flow, contingency and cascading failure studies and grid planning. Related records: platform-dynawo provides dynamic simulation within the same ecosystem.
